Andrew Bonar
BON-er
proper noun
From the surname Bonar; a nineteenth-century Free Church of Scotland minister, brother of Horatius Bonar and biographer of Robert Murray M’Cheyne.

📖 Biblical Definition

Andrew Bonar was a minister of the Free Church of Scotland in the nineteenth century, brother of the hymn-writer Horatius Bonar, and one of the most saintly men of his age. He is best remembered as the biographer of his friend Robert Murray M’Cheyne, whose Memoir and Remains, gathered by Bonar, has stirred more men to holiness and to the love of Christ than almost any book of its kind. Bonar himself was a man of deep prayer and Christ-filled devotion, whose diary breathes a continual longing after God and a tender walk with the Saviour. His Commentary on Leviticus opened to many the gospel hidden in the sacrifices, that it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul (Lev 17:11). The dictionary honours Bonar as a pastor of rare holiness who followed peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord (Heb 12:14), and whose one desire was that of Paul, that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings (Php 3:10). He walked in the light as God is in the light, knowing that the blood of Jesus Christ cleanseth from all sin (1Jo 1:7). His life and his pen alike pressed upon the church the pursuit of holiness and the nearness of the believing soul to Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A nineteenth-century Free Church of Scotland minister, biographer of M’Cheyne and a man of rare holiness.

ANDREW BONAR, a nineteenth-century Free Church of Scotland minister.

He was the brother of the hymn-writer Horatius Bonar.

He wrote the Memoir of Robert Murray M’Cheyne.

His Commentary on Leviticus opened the gospel in the sacrifices.

He was a man of deep prayer and Christ-filled devotion.

📖 Key Scripture

Lev 17:11 — "For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul."

Heb 12:14 — "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:"

Php 3:10 — "That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;"

1Jo 1:7 — "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

He pressed upon the church the pursuit of holiness and the nearness of the soul to Christ, the blood of the Lamb its atonement.

expand to see more

What is honourable in Andrew Bonar is his rare holiness and his Christ-filled devotion. In an age of growing coldness and busy religion, he kept a near and tender walk with the Saviour, and his Memoir of M’Cheyne and his own diary have stirred countless souls to follow after holiness. The dictionary honours this pastor of prayer, whose one desire was to know Christ and the power of His resurrection.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the principle to recover is the pursuit of holiness and the nearness of the believing soul to Christ. Bonar opened in Leviticus the gospel of the atoning blood, for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul, and pressed upon the church that we follow holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. He walked in the light as God is in the light, resting in the blood of Jesus that cleanseth from all sin. His life rebukes a religion content with orthodoxy without communion, and calls the saints to know Christ and to be made conformable unto His death.
